summary: American Girl Mine BLM dispersed: BLM El Centro FO page + its Eastern Imperial County routes brochure + BLM SMA + Esri. No BLM page names or designates camping at American Girl Mine; the brochure only permits dispersed vehicle camping anywhere within 300 ft of designated routes. Pin is on BLM land. 14-day/28-day limit confirmed. Drop candidate: dispersed area with no agency designation.
flags: DROP CANDIDATE (dispersed area with no agency designation): no blm.gov page, recreation-site listing or brochure names American Girl Mine (or Ogilby Road) as a camping area. The El Centro Field Office's 'Routes of Travel for Eastern Imperial County' brochure only says 'Camping opportunities can be found throughout the public lands administered by the BLM ... generally do not have signs marking them as campsites' and 'vehicle camping is allowed within 300 feet of designated routes of travel'. That is blanket permission, not a designation, the same position as Homestake Pass 6071 and Rito Hondo. Named camping here rests on aggregators (The Dyrt, lets-see-america.com, RV Life). Nearest BLM-designated alternative: Pilot Knob LTVA (https://www.blm.gov/visit/search-details/15080/2), ~25 km SE; it is likely already in the DB, not checked.

Land status: BLM's surface-management map puts the pin on BLM land; one Dyrt reviewer reports camping on land owned by the adjacent mine. Rule 5 bars camping within 1 mile of an LTVA; the pin is not near one.
Fees $0 not restated by the agency source (the brochure is silent on fees); left as stored.

Website https://www.blm.gov/office/el-centro-field-office is the generic field-office page. If kept, a better source is the brochure https://www.blm.gov/sites/blm.gov/files/docs/2021-03/EasternImperialCountyNECO-REV2020-121820_508.pdf. Phone 760-337-4400 confirmed (brochure and office page).
Pin 32.8368,-114.812 is on American Girl Mine Rd; no move.
No closure found (the office page's only closure link is Osborne, a different area).
